# Ideogram Precise Edit Gets a Full-Res Context Window

Aurelia

AureliaOctober 29, 2026

Image Gen News

## Introduction

Ideogram has upgraded Precise Edit on its Ideogram 4.5 image model with a context window. You pick a region of up to roughly 2K (4.19 megapixels) inside a much larger image, and only that region is edited at its original pixels. Every pixel outside the window comes back exactly as you sent it, at the image's full width and height. It's a closed, API-served model available today in the Ideogram app, the Ideogram API, and partner platforms including fal, Runware, Runway, Luma, Luminal, ComfyUI, and Scenario. [...] The context window takes a different approach. Instead of shrinking the whole image, the model works only on the window at native resolution and stitches it back in. Ideogram's pitch is "no seams, no artifacts, no Photoshop," with small text, logos, and fine detail rendered more sharply.

## How the Context Window Works

The new field is `context_window` on `POST /v2/image/precise-edit/ideogram-4-5`, and it has three modes:

 `none` (default): Edits the whole image. Anything over 2048×2048 in area is scaled down.
 `auto`: Needs a mask. Ideogram fits a window around the masked area, and the output keeps the full resolution.
 `y_min,x_min,y_max,x_max`: You name the window by corner pixels, rows first. A mask is optional, but any black mask area must fall inside the window. [...] Precise Edit itself isn't new. We covered the Ideogram 4.5 precise multi-turn edits launch in September. The news here is resolution: until now, big images had to shrink before they could be edited.

## The Problem It Fixes

Editing the whole image is still capped at 4,194,304 pixels, the area of a 2048×2048 square. Ideogram's API docs give a blunt example: send an 8192×8192 image with the default `context_window=none` and it comes back as 2048×2048. Ideogram's launch page shows the same thing with a 4K product label that returns at 2K without a context window. With a window, the result stays at 4K.

# Precise Edit with context window

Make surgical edits with context window in images up to 8K. You no longer have to downscale to edit, or stitch crops back with border and color artifacts.

You can edit any area up to 2K at its original pixels. Everything outside the context window stays untouched, so your image keeps its original resolution, with no seam and no color mismatch.

Try Precise Edit API doc

With and without a context window

## The context window also improves editing quality in fine detail.

### Without a context window

The 4K original is scaled down to edit, so the result comes back at 2K. [...] `context_window=none`
  :   Edit the whole image. Over 2048 × 2048 pixels of area, it comes back scaled down to fit. This is the default.

  `context_window=auto`
  :   Fit the window around the mask, so the edit keeps the image's full resolution.

  `context_window=y_min,x_min,y_max,x_max`
  :   Set the window yourself, by its corner pixels, rows first. Each side is at least 256 px, the area is at most 2048 × 2048, and the aspect ratio stays within 6:1.

## One field sets where the model works.

`context_window` names a region of the image. The model edits that region at its original pixels and places it back, and every pixel outside it returns exactly as sent. A mask inside the window narrows the edit to the pixels that may change.

 ### Precise Edit

  `POST /v2/image/precise-edit/ideogram-4-5`

  Send the image and a prompt, with a mask, a context\_window, or both. The response is the full image at its own size.

🖼️ Fix one corner of a giant image and leave every other pixel alone.  
  
Ideogram just launched a context window for precise edits. You pick an area up to 2K inside a very high-resolution image and edit only that part. Everything outside the window stays untouched. Ideogram's own pitch: "No seams, no artifacts, no Photoshop!"  
  
What's new, per Ideogram's launch post:  
✅ Edit any area up to 2K inside very high-resolution images  
✅ Everything outside the context window stays untouched  
✅ Available now in the Ideogram app and the API  
  
My take (opinion): big print files, posters and product shots are where AI editing usually falls apart, because you end up regenerating the whole thing. Editing a small window is how designers actually work.
